bib.title: InternVL: Scaling up Vision Foundation Models and Aligning for Generic Visual-Linguistic Tasks

question: Can a vision encoder scaled to 6B parameters, progressively aligned with an LLM-initialised middleware, serve both contrastive and generative vision-language tasks?
hypothesis: Scaling the vision encoder to match LLM scale and aligning its representation with an LLM (rather than a light glue layer) gives better visual and vision-language performance.
contributions: A large-scale vision-language foundation model aligning a 6B vision encoder with LLMs
A progressive image-text alignment strategy (contrastive on noisy data, then generative on cleaned data)
Extensive comparison with SoTA vision foundation models and VLLMs

method.summary: InternViT-6B (vanilla ViT, patch 14) is trained contrastively against a multilingual LLaMA-7B text encoder (stage 1), then frozen and joined to QLLaMA (LLaMA-7B plus 96 learnable queries and cross-attention, 8B total) with ITC+ITM+ITG losses (stage 2), then connected to Vicuna/InternLM through an MLP for SFT (stage 3). Images are fixed-square resized (224 pretraining, 336 for chat SFT), not tiled.
